claims.claim_text: The private identifier printed for James C. Burwell resolves to an official Army record with a different middle initial, so the indexed identity remains conflicting.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Exact identifier comparison produced the same first and last names but a conflicting middle initial; the identifier and unassigned Army details are withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The private identifier is strong linkage evidence, but C versus S is a direct name conflict that no independent reviewed source resolves.
claims.temporal_assessment: The conflicting Army record cannot safely establish the indexed person's chronology, occupation, or employment.
claims.match_notes: No Army category, entry status, occupation, employer, or chronology is transferred pending comparison with Box 96. Same-name newspaper, directory, military, obituary, cemetery, and modern candidates lacked the private identifier or folder linkage.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Charles C. Busenkell is a high-confidence match to the United States Naval Reserve lieutenant commander who led the OSS Special Projects Office Electronics Section from October 1944 to October 1945.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Officer-in-Charge of the Electronics Section, Special Projects Office, Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A person-specific Legion of Merit citation names the exact uncommon full name, naval rank, OSS office, leadership role, and service dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match from the exact uncommon full name and direct, person-specific OSS award citation; the original Box 96 file has not been compared.
claims.temporal_assessment: The citation documents an OSS role from October 1944 through October 1945. It does not identify his immediately preceding naval assignment or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: A 1940 amateur-radio callbook and a 1960 engineering directory are identity or career leads only; neither establishes a pre-OSS employer or immediate predecessor. The award page's service number is intentionally omitted.
